requirement.original: 检修 Spec Item 5.3 — Right sidebar detail panel lacks horizontal overflow handling. Long commands overflow popup width.
requirement.clarified: Make Bash tool-call command text fully visible inside the right detail popup (SidebarBashView) at desktop 1440x900 AND mobile 390x844. Cycle 1's CommandView style change stays for BashViewFull/CodexBashView; only SidebarBashView switches from horizontal-scroll to soft-wrap.
requirement.what: Add an opt-in wrap prop to CommandView and remove the horizontal ScrollView from SidebarBashView so the command wraps within the 450/390 popup boundary instead of relying on a touch-only scroll affordance that is invisible at rest on web.
requirement.why: Cycle 1's L1 fix correctly enables horizontal scroll mathematically, but the user-facing requirement (command stays inside popup) is not satisfied because the horizontal scrollbar is invisible at rest on web. User cannot read the rest of the command without knowing to drag-scroll a hidden affordance.

included: Right detail panel (SidebarBashView) Bash tool-call rendering
excluded: CodexBashView — out of scope, separate spec item §5.6
Any change to message-list horizontal layout outside the popup

success_criteria: At viewport 1440x900, no DOM element inside the right-panel container has bounding-rect right greater than the panel's right edge.
At viewport 390x844, no DOM element inside the [role="dialog"] modal has bounding-rect right greater than 390.
BashViewFull and CodexBashView source files show zero changes after this cycle's commit.
constraints: Do NOT re-introduce flexWrap: 'wrap' UNCONDITIONALLY on CommandView line style — must be opt-in via the new wrap prop.
Do NOT re-introduce flex: 1 on commandText — use flexShrink: 1 instead when wrap is true.
wordBreak: 'break-all' is web-only; gate via Platform.OS === 'web'.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Long Bash command text in the right detail popup appears cut off at the popup boundary with no visible scrollbar on web (both mobile and desktop).
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: SidebarBashView wraps CommandView in a horizontal ScrollView (overflow-x: auto on the underlying div). On web Chrome, the horizontal scrollbar is touch-only / hover-only and invisible at rest, so the command APPEARS to overflow. The scroll DOES technically work — clientWidth=390 vs scrollWidth=1109 — but is undiscoverable.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Cycle 1 spec ba-spec-20260424-143000-4.md chose horizontal-scroll as the implementation for §5.3 acceptance point 2 ("Acceptable implementations: horizontal scroll within the command code block, soft-wrap at word boundaries, or responsive truncation"). Math-wise the implementation is correct; UX-wise the affordance is invisible.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: User experience is identical to pre-fix: command appears overflowing the popup with no visible scrollbar to communicate scrollability. Cycle 5 QA initially marked PASS (depth-5 ancestor has overflow-x: auto). Audit overturned this — even though the scroll math works, the user-facing acceptance criterion ("command stays inside popup") is not met.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Cycle 1 (2026-04-24): horizontal-scroll fix landed. Cycle 5 (2026-04-25 ~13:00Z): QA reported PASS. Cycle 5 audit (2026-04-25 ~15:00Z): user feedback overturned PASS. This cycle (2026-04-25 ~20:00Z): retry with L2 structural change.

attempts.proposed_solution: Remove flexWrap: 'wrap' from CommandView.tsx:45 and flex: 1 from CommandView commandText style at line 59. Add horizontal ScrollView wrapper to CodexBashView bash branch.
attempts.actual_change: CommandView.tsx line and commandText styles modified as proposed; CodexBashView ScrollView added.
attempts.outcome: Cycle 5 self-PASS (desktop) overturned by user + audit. Horizontal scroll math works (depth-5 has clientWidth=390, scrollWidth=1109, overflow-x: auto), but the scroll affordance is invisible on web at rest. User still perceives command as overflowing popup with no way to read the rest.

novelty_check.rationale: Cycle 1 changed two CSS properties on the shared CommandView. This cycle (a) modifies SidebarBashView's structural rendering — removes the horizontal ScrollView wrapper entirely — and (b) adds a NEW prop to CommandView (additive, not a property removal). Both target file (SidebarBashView is primary) and layer (L2 structural component-contract change vs L1 cosmetic CSS change) differ from cycle 1. The prior failure mode (invisible scroll affordance) cannot recur because there is no horizontal scroll on the popup post-fix — content wraps inside the popup boundary.
